title: Laxative treatment perturbs gut microbiome composition and metabolism in humans independent of short-term fiber consumption: a randomized controlled crossover intervention study.
abstract: Gastrointestinal transit time is a major ecological determinant of the human gut microbiome, yet causal evidence that disentangles the effects of diet from those of the gut environment remains limited. Here, we conducted a randomized, controlled crossover trial in healthy adults (nine females, four males) consuming fully standardized high-fiber (40 g/d) or low-fiber (10 g/d) diets to assess how manipulating the gut environment using an osmotic laxative (Movicol) affects gut microbial composition

title: Microbiota-Bile acid decoupling contributes to altered postnatal growth and metabolism in sFGR: a twin-paired dynamic study with FMT validation.
abstract: Selective fetal growth restriction (sFGR) increases the risk of adverse long-term metabolic outcomes, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Bile acids (BAs) mediate gut microbiota-host metabolic crosstalk, and their early-life perturbation may underlie sFGR-associated health risks. Using a monochorionic diamniotic twin cohort (25 concordant pairs, 22 sFGR pairs), we developed a twin-specific analytical framework integrating birth weight deviation, intra-pair difference, and time-weighted

title: Modulation of neuroimmunity by early-life microbiota colonization.
abstract: Early life (fetal period to 2-3 y postnatally) is a critical window for the coordinated development of the intestine, lungs, and brain. As core pathways mediating microbe-immune-neuron crosstalk, the gut-brain and lung-brain axes drive cross-organ communication via early-life microbiota colonization, profoundly shaping immune maturation and neurodevelopmental trajectories. During fetal development, maternal microbial metabolites cross the placenta to prime in utero immune and neural development.

title: Gut Holdemania filiformis raises brain isoallopregnanolone in progesterone-treated female mice.
abstract: Neuroactive 5α-steroids modulate γ-aminobutyric acid type A (GABAA) receptor signaling and are of growing therapeutic interest: allopregnanolone (3α,5α) is a positive allosteric modulator, whereas its 3β-epimer isoallopregnanolone antagonizes this action and is itself in clinical development. Their formation has been attributed to host enzymes in the liver, gastrointestinal tract, and central nervous system, whereas a contribution from any individual gut bacterium has not been demonstrated. title: Helicobacter pylori in the pediatric gastric niche: from pathobiont to pathogen and the pre-adolescent window of opportunity.
abstract: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) is a definitive adult carcinogen, yet pediatric management remains conservative due to the rarity of acute complications. This review addresses a paradigm shift, evaluating whether H. pylori behaves as a tolerated pathobiont or an active pathogen within the pediatric gastric niche. title: Gut microbiome patterns in a multi-ethnic Asian population within a shared urban environment.
abstract: The gut microbiome composition varies across human populations, but its characteristics and determinants in a multi-ethnic setting remain incompletely understood. Singapore, a multicultural city-state, provides a context in which culturally diverse groups share a broadly similar built environment. Using the Health for Life in Singapore (HELIOS) cohort, we profiled the gut microbiome of ethnic Chinese, Indian, and Malay participants (n = 861) residing in the country. title: Ultrahigh-Temperature Processing Reduces miR-26a in Bovine Milk Exosomes and Weakens Their Anti-Inflammatory Activity by Impairing TAK1-MAPK Suppression and Gut Microbiota Modulation.
abstract: Ultrahigh-temperature (UHT) sterilization ensures dairy safety, but its effects on the biological activity of bovine milk exosomes (BMEs) remain unclear. Using a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis mouse model, we compared raw milk exosomes (Raw_MEs), UHT-treated exosomes (UHT_MEs), and bta-miR-26a-loaded liposomes (MiR_Lipo). journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Sodium butyrate combined with ethanol-metabolizing Lactobacillus strains attenuates alcoholic liver disease by restoring gut-liver homeostasis.
abstract: Alcoholic liver disease (ALD) is characterized by hepatic lipid accumulation, inflammation, and intestinal barrier dysfunction, while limited effective pharmacological interventions remain currently available. This study investigated the protective effects of sodium butyrate (NaB), alone and in combination with newly isolated ethanol-metabolizing Lactobacillus strains on ALD, and examined the contribution of the gut microbiota. title: Fermented Polygonatum kingianum polysaccharide exerts enhanced anti-obesity effects by modulating the gut microbiota-GDCA-TGR5 axis.
abstract: Probiotic-fermented Polygonatum kingianum polysaccharide (FPKP0) was previously confirmed to exhibit enhanced anti-adipogenic activity in 3T3-L1 cells in vitro owing to altered structural, prompting an examination of whether this modified FPKP0 exerts superior anti-obesity effects in vivo via related mechanism in high-fat diet-fed mice. journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology

title: Camellia nitidissima Chi flower extract ameliorates alcoholic liver disease by reshaping bile acid homeostasis and intestinal barrier function.
abstract: Bile acid (BA) dyshomeostasis and intestinal barrier dysfunction are critical drivers of alcoholic liver disease (ALD), for which effective pharmacotherapies remain limited. Although Camellia nitidissima Chi flower possesses anti-inflammatory, hepatoprotective, and microbiota-modulatory properties, its role in ALD remains unclear.
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology

title: Nutritional interventions in neonatal sepsis prevention & treatment.
abstract: Neonatal sepsis remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, particularly among preterm infants with profound immune, metabolic, and gastrointestinal immaturity. Optimizing nutrition represents a promising yet complex strategy to support immune function, preserve gut integrity, and improve outcomes in this high-risk population. This narrative review explores the interplay between neonatal sepsis, inflammation, and nutrition, with a focus on the roles of human milk, parenteral nu

title: A Potential Probiotic Candidate Heyndrickxia ginsengihumi W1 is Associated with Increased Intestinal Stem Cell-Mediated Proliferation and Altered Barrier-Related Parameters: Potential Involvement of the Wnt/β-Catenin Pathway.
abstract: Probiotic properties of the rumen-derived strain Heyndrickxia ginsengihumi W1 were evaluated by whole-genome analysis, in vitro assays, and a short-term mouse model. Genome analysis preliminarily indicated no acquired antimicrobial resistance genes or virulence factors. In mice, W1 administration showed no obvious adverse effects under the present short-term experimental conditions, and was associated with Lactobacillus enrichment and elevated lactate in the jejunum. journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Characterization of potential probiotic Lactobacillus spp. isolated from commercially reared pigs.
abstract: Probiotic bacteria and their products have shown significant promise as alternatives to traditional antimicrobials in the pig husbandry due to their antimicrobial activity. This study describes the comprehensive characterization of potential probiotic isolates sourced from the feces of commercial pig herds. Using high-throughput screening methodologies, sequential tests were performed, and isolates were discarded following any failure to meet a test acceptance criterion, allowing the initial 81

title: [Research progress on the mechanism of acupuncture in protecting the intestinal barrier to intervene in Parkinson's disease].
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder worldwide. Accumulating evidence from recent years indicates a strong association between PD pathogenesis and gut-brain axis dysfunction, with impairment of the intestinal barrier being recognized as a critical initiating factor. This review summarizes current research on the multi-target mechanisms through which acupuncture protects the intestinal barrier and thereby intervenes in PD progression. Evidence suggests tha

title: Lactobacillus-derived threonine mediates the protective effect of piceatannol against endometritis.
abstract: Bacterial endometritis reflects a convergence of persistent infection, barrier failure, and excessive inflammation, yet how the gut microbiota influences these processes remains poorly understood. Here, we show that piceatannol (PIC) alleviates Escherichia coli-induced endometritis through a microbiota-dependent mechanism that limits uterine injury and preserves epithelial barrier function. title: Fecal microbiota transplantation modulates immunosuppressive cells and IgA secretion in a gut microbiota depletion model.
abstract: The relationship between gut dysbiosis and host immune dynamics remains poorly understood. We used an antibiotic-induced gut microbiota depletion model following fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) via co-housing. Mice received an antibiotic cocktail for 4 weeks (Abx group), or for 2 weeks, followed by co-housing with healthy control mice for 2 weeks (CoA group), or kept under conventional housing for 2 weeks (Abx-CH group). title: Discovery of Human Gut Bacteria Responsible for Biotransformation and Structural Diversification of Oat Steroidal Saponins.
abstract: Oat steroidal saponins undergo biotransformation by the gut microbiota, yet the bacteria involved and the structural diversity of the resulting metabolites remain incompletely characterized. Incubation of avenacoside B (AVE-B), a major oat steroidal saponin, with fecal microbiota from six human donors revealed marked interindividual variation in avenacoside E (AVE-E) production. Five bacterial species capable of AVE-B metabolism were isolated, with Bacteroides uniformis SS-F-0001 exhibiting the
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Vagus nerve stimulation ameliorates epilepsy via a gut microbiota-butyrate-vagal axis.
abstract: Vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) is a therapy for drug-resistant epilepsy, yet its mechanisms are incompletely understood. We demonstrate that VNS modulates the gut microbiome and alters butyrate levels to reduce seizure susceptibility via vagus nerve-dependent signaling. In a longitudinal cohort of patients with epilepsy, VNS enriched short-chain fatty acid-producing bacteria, including Akkermansia muciniphila, Prevotella, Alistipes, and Odoribacter. title: Acetate-FFAR2 signaling induces neutrophil-derived IL-22 to protect against colitis.
abstract: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) produced by gut microbiota are key modulators of intestinal homeostasis and immune responses. Although their anti-inflammatory roles are well established, the mechanisms by which SCFAs-FFAR2 shapes neutrophil function and influences intestinal inflammation remain unclear. Here, we demonstrate that dietary fiber or acetate protect mice from DSS-induced colitis despite increasing neutrophil infiltration into the intestinal tissue. Importantly, neutrophils are requir
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

title: Lactate-induced PRDX1 lactylation increases the number of IgA plasma cells to confer exercise-mimicking protection against IBD.
abstract: Regular exercise enhances immune fitness and reduces disease risk; however, how it mobilizes immunity for disease prevention and key therapeutic targets remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a gut IgA-producing plasma cell subset (FSPhigh IgA PCs) that is functionally induced by exercise and characterized by high expression of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-related genes Fkbp11, Ssr2, and Ppib (collectively FSP). Exercise expands ER architecture and capacity in these FSPhigh IgA PCs, enabl

title: Dysbiosis in the gut microbiota and arginine and proline metabolism is associated with cognitive decline in aging.
abstract: Aging represents a severe health concern and causes various manifestations including neurodegeneration and metabolic dysfunction. The gut-brain axis has been implicated in cognitive aging. However, the associations of specific gut microbiota and metabolites with age-related cognitive decline remain poorly defined.

title: Neuroinflammation in Parkinson's disease: from glial heterogeneity and gut-brain immune crosstalk to precision therapeutic strategies.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuronal loss, α-synuclein pathology, and a broad spectrum of motor and non-motor manifestations. Neuroinflammation is increasingly recognized as an important component of PD pathobiology; however, traditional frameworks have largely focused on canonical inflammatory pathways and simplified classifications of glial activation, which do not fully capture the spatial, temporal, and functional heterog

title: Cutaneous SCFAs are reduced in infantile atopic dermatitis and the SCFA-sensing receptor GPR43 modulates skin barrier integrity and inflammation.
abstract: Early-life skin colonization by commensal microbes is associated with a reduced risk of atopic dermatitis (AD), but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Regulatory effects of commensal gut bacteria are mediated in part by short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), metabolites generated during fiber fermentation. title: Fermented Sasa quelpaertensis-Supplemented Milk Attenuates UVB-Induced Skin Photoaging and Alters Gut Microbial and Short-Chain Fatty Acid Profiles.
abstract: Ultraviolet B (UVB) exposure accelerates skin photoaging by promoting extracellular matrix degradation, inflammatory responses, and epidermal barrier dysfunction. This study investigated the protective effects of Sasa quelpaertensis-supplemented milk (MSQ) and fermented S. quelpaertensis-supplemented milk (FMSQ), prepared using Lactobacillus gasseri KML25, in UVB-exposed HaCaT keratinocytes and SKH-1 hairless mice. In HaCaT cells, FMSQ suppressed UVB-induced phosphorylation of extracellular sign

title: Role of Bile Acids in Colorectal Diseases.
abstract: Bile acids (BAs) have functions well beyond fat digestion. They also serve as signals linking the gut microbiota to gut health. This review examines how BAs affect colorectal diseases and how this knowledge can guide diagnosis and treatment.

title: Perinatal deficiency in vitamin B9 and B12 is associated with gut dysbiosis, impaired serotonin-kynurenine pathways and is linked to psychiatric-like disorders in rat offspring.
abstract: The prevalence of neurodegenerative diseases and psychiatric disorders, including anxiety and depression, appears to be higher among patients with gastrointestinal diseases, supporting the existence of a functional communication in the "gut-brain axis", that remains poorly described. title: The inhibitory effect and mechanism of allicin combined with propolis extract on Cryptosporidiumparvum.
abstract: This study investigated the therapeutic potential of allicin combined with ethanolic propolis extract (ABP) and allicin combined with aqueous propolis extract (AWBP) against cryptosporidiosis. Results of molecular docking indicated that ABP could efficiently target the active pockets of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and ATP translocase in C. parvum, and stably bind to key amino acid residues through hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions. title: Indole-3-lactic acid from gut microbiota suppresses colorectal cancer through AHR-ZBP1 signaling and PANoptosis-like cell death.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health burden. This study observed reduced relative abundance of sequences assigned to Roseburia inulinivorans in patients with CRC. R. inulinivorans-derived cell-free supernatant (CFS) reduced CRC cell viability and clonogenic capacity and decreased tumor burden in an azoxymethane/dextran sulfate sodium model. title: Microbiota-gut-brain Axis in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Mechanistic Insights, Experimental and Clinical Evidence, and Therapeutic Perspectives.
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition characterized by marked biological and clinical heterogeneity, arising from an interplay of genetic vulnerability, immune, metabolic, and gastrointestinal dysfunction, and neurobiological alterations. The bidirectional communication between the gut microbiota and the brain via neural, immune, endocrine, and microbial- metabolite pathways may contribute to ASD pathophysiology. title: Maternal gluten diet exacerbates offspring autistic-like behaviors through the gut-brain axis mediated by gut microbial metabolite elaidic acid.
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous group of neurodevelopmental conditions characterized by social deficits and stereotyped behaviors, for which effective treatments remain lacking. Here we investigated whether early-life gluten exposure exacerbates autism-like behaviors in BTBR mice and explored the underlying microbiota-metabolite-brain mechanism. Early-life gluten exposure aggravated social avoidance, anxiety, and repetitive behaviors in BTBR offspring, accompanied by reduced mu

title: High-throughput screening of patient iPSC-derived neurons identifies the gut microbial metabolites that attenuate Alzheimer's disease pathology.
abstract: Gut microbiota-derived metabolites influence the gut-brain axis and may impact Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology. However, the microbial metabolites involved in this process and their functional roles are largely unknown. We screened 352 gut metabolites in induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC)-derived neurons from individuals with AD to identify compounds that reduce tau hyperphosphorylation. title: Formation of an inulin biocorona on food-grade titanium dioxide nanoparticles alleviates gut microbiota dysbiosis and inflammatory responses under calorie restriction.
abstract: Food-grade nanoparticles undergo dynamic interactions with dietary biomolecules during gastrointestinal transit, leading to the formation of a biomolecular corona that determines their biological identity and health effects. Here, we investigated whether an inulin-derived biocorona could modulate the gastrointestinal fate and biological responses of the nanoscale fraction of titanium dioxide (TiO2) under normal and calorie-restricted conditions. title: A NanAKE-like pathway enables sialic acid catabolism in gut microbiome member Hungatella hathewayi.
abstract: Sialic acids are abundant components of host- and diet-derived glycans in the human gut that shape microbial fitness and interspecies competition. Free sialic acids can be a nutrient source but also stimulate inflammation and pathogen colonization. Escherichia coli and Bacteroides spp. catabolize sialic acids via the NanAKE and NanLE-RokA pathways, yet the metabolic capacity of many microbiome members remains undefined. title: Diet correction after perinatal deficiency in vitamin B9 and B12 fails to rescue gut dysbiosis, serotonin pathway and psychiatric-like behavior in adult rats.
abstract: Perinatal dietary deficiencies such as vitamin B9 and B12 induce persistent gut dysbiosis, metabolic, physiologic imbalances and behavioral defects that could extend into adulthood, but the underlying fetal programming mechanisms remain poorly understood. We have investigated the long-term consequences of a perinatal vitamin B9 and B12 deficiency associated dysbiosis and focusing on sex-dependent outcomes related to behavior and molecular markers of the gut-brain axis. title: Primary sclerosing cholangitis: epidemiology, risk factors, pathophysiology, clinical features, diagnosis, and management.
abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a rare cholangiopathy characterized by multifocal inflammation and fibrostenotic remodeling of the bile ducts, cholestasis, and increased risks of cholangiocarcinoma and colorectal cancer. No pharmacological therapy has yet improved transplant-free survival. Clinical care therefore depends on accurate phenotyping, surveillance, treatment of biliary and intestinal complications, and timely liver transplantation. title: BGN4-derived intestinal metabolite 6-hydroxynicotinic acid alleviates hepatocytes ferroptosis in MAFLD via Nrf2/SREBP1/CYP2E1 axis.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is closely associated with dysbiosis of the gut microbiota. In this study, we investigated the biological effects and underlying mechanisms of Bifidobacterium bifidum BGN4 and its intestinal metabolite, 6-hydroxynicotinic acid (6-HNA), in regulating hepatocyte ferroptosis in MAFLD.
journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences

title: Lactobacillus plantarum CCFM639 attenuates high-salt-induced hypertension involving IL-17A signaling suppression.
abstract: Chronic high-salt (HS) intake induces hypertension and is associated with reduced intestinal Lactobacillus. This study investigated underlying mechanisms for Lactobacillus plantarum CCFM639 (CCFM639) alleviating HS-induced hypertension.

title: The Gut Microbiota: A Critical Mediator in Particulate Matter-Induced Health Risks.
abstract: Environmental particulate matter (PM), particularly fine particles (PM2.5), coarse particles (PM10), and ultrafine particles (UFPs), pose a major public health threat. Emerging evidence identifies the gut microbiota as a key mediator through which PM exposure induces systemic health effects. Exposure to PM disrupts microbial diversity and structure throughout the life cycle. This disruption is characterized by a loss of beneficial microbes and an increase in potentially harmful ones. title: Gut microbiota-driven imbalance of the gut-brain-immune homeostatic network in constipation: Pathogenic mechanisms and evolving therapeutic prospects.
abstract: Chronic constipation (CC) is increasingly recognized as a systems-level disorder that cannot be explained by impaired intestinal motility alone. Here, we integrate evidence from clinical cohorts, animal models, and mechanistic studies to examine how gut microbial dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolites perturb epithelial barrier integrity, immune homeostasis, enteric neural activity, and gut-brain signaling. title: Salinity-Driven Nonadditive Disruption of Digestive Energy Homeostasis in Mussels by Titanium Dioxide Nanoparticles.
abstract: Titanium dioxide nanoparticles (TiO2 NPs) are increasingly accumulating in coastal waters. Seasonal salinity fluctuations further complicate their ecological risks. We investigated how salinity modulates TiO2 NP toxicity on digestive energy metabolism in the thick-shelled mussel Mytilus coruscus, an important coastal economic shellfish. title: Prebiotic Potential of Codonopsis lanceolata Root Peel Extract: Attenuation of DSS-Induced Colitis Associated with Selective Modulation of the Gut Microbiota.
abstract: Codonopsis lanceolata root peel, which is commonly discarded as an agro-industrial byproduct, was investigated as a potential source of gut health-promoting components. The present study evaluated the intestinal protective effects and growth-supporting potential of an aqueous C. lanceolata root peel extract (CPE). title: Isolation, identification and prebiotic potential of polysaccharides from fresh goji berry.
abstract: Polysaccharides from fresh goji berry were isolated and characterized to investigate their structures, simulated gastrointestinal digestion, and lactic acid bacteria (LAB) growth-supporting effects. Hot-water extraction, 50% ethanol precipitation, and chromatographic separation yielded two acidic polysaccharides, LBP1 and LBP2, with apparent molecular weights of 13.47 ± 0.24 and 185.0 ± 3.0 kDa, respectively. title: Ovarian function via gut microbiota-driven serotonin dysregulation in zebrafish.
abstract: Ciprofloxacin (CIP) is frequently detected in aquatic environments, yet its effects on reproduction through gut microbiota-mediated pathways remain unclear. Adult female zebrafish were exposed to 5,000 ng/L CIP for 30 days and evaluated using histology, hormone assays, metagenomics, metabolomics, transcriptomics, and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT). title: High-throughput screening identifies Limosilactobacillus reuteri HBNK04 as a potent antiviral probiotic against porcine epidemic diarrhea virus.
abstract: Porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) continues to cause substantial economic losses to the swine industry, and current vaccines and biosecurity measures remain insufficient to prevent viral spread. Probiotics have emerged as promising microecological interventions due to their capacity to inhibit pathogens and modulate host immunity. In this study, 194 Limosilactobacillus reuteri (L. reuteri) isolates from healthy pigs were screened using a "Cell-probiotic-PEDV" tri-component platform, and str

title: Oral live and heat-killed Ligilactobacillus salivarius Ls.0403 alleviate MC903-induced atopic dermatitis-like inflammation and are associated with gut microbiota changes in mice.
abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory skin disease that often requires long-term management. Probiotics have been investigated as adjunctive approaches for AD, but their effects are highly strain specific. Among these, Ligilactobacillus salivarius has shown potential in previous AD studies, yet the effects of different strains remain insufficiently characterized. In this study, we screened 19 human-derived L. salivarius isolates and selected Ls.0403, which exhibited favorab

title: Microbiome-dependent phytosterol sulfates production and tissue distribution in mice.
abstract: Microbial biotransformation of dietary lipids, such as cholesterol, influences host homeostasis. Despite extensive studies on animal sterols in host-microbiota interactions, the role of phytosterols in homeostasis remains unclear. In this study, we characterized phytosterol sulfates as microbiota-derived metabolites using untargeted lipidomic data mining. title: Gut microbiota composition of India's Baiga tribe: Insights from an indigenous particularly vulnerable tribal group.
abstract: The transition from traditional foraging lifestyles to modernized urban environments is associated with reduced human gut microbiome diversity. To examine this shift within the Indian subcontinent, we used shotgun metagenomics to compare the gut microbiota of 50 adults: 25 from the indigenous, foraging, and particularly vulnerable Baiga tribe and 25 from an urban population in Bhopal, Central India. title: EndD mediates butyrate-dependent toxin release and sporulation in Clostridioides difficile.
abstract: Clostridioides difficile is an urgent threat to human health. Current treatments for C. difficile infections (CDIs) are antibiotics and microbiome restoration therapy (MRT) for recurrent cases. However, antibiotics contribute to antibiotic resistance and recurrent CDIs, and the long-term sustainability and accessibility of MRTs remain to be determined. title: An HA-Coated Akkermansia-Paeoniflorin Biohybrid Enables Sustained Oral Delivery for Gut-Gonad Axis Protection.
abstract: Living biohybrid materials offer a unique opportunity to couple oral drug delivery with host-microbiome interactions, yet maintaining carrier integrity, cargo retention, and biological function under gastrointestinal constraints remains challenging. Here, we engineered a hyaluronic acid (HA)-coated Akkermansia muciniphila-paeoniflorin biohybrid (PF@AKK@HA) through vacuum-enabled paeoniflorin loading followed by HA shell stabilization. title: Distinct Probiotic Effects of Limosilactobacillus fermentum Perfectus001 and Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis Perfectus006 in a Rat Model of Spleen qi Deficiency Syndrome.
abstract: Spleen qi deficiency syndrome (SDS) is characterized by chronic fatigue, gastrointestinal dysfunction, and systemic metabolic disturbances and has been associated with gut microbial dysbiosis and chronic inflammation. This study evaluated the effects of two probiotic strains, Limosilactobacillus fermentum Perfectus001 (LFP) and Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis Perfectus006 (BAP), in an SDS rat model. title: The role of the gut microbiome in stress responses of dogs: gut-brain axis and microbiome-targeted interventions.
abstract: Stress poses a significant threat to canine welfare and adoptability, particularly in animal shelters where dogs are exposed to multiple environmental and social stressors. Growing evidence suggests that the gut-brain axis (GBA), a bidirectional communication network linking the gastrointestinal tract and the central nervous system, plays a critical role in regulating stress responses. journal: The Journal of veterinary medical science

title: Alterations in the gut microbiome of dogs with acute diarrhea.
abstract: To investigate differences in the intestinal microbiota between dogs with acute diarrhea and healthy dogs, this study included 10 dogs with acute diarrhea (acute diarrhea group) and 10 healthy dogs (healthy control group). High-throughput sequencing of the V3-V4 region of the 16S rRNA gene, combined with bioinformatic analysis, was used to analyze microbial diversity, taxonomic composition, and predicted functional profiles of the intestinal microbiota. title: Antibiotic heteroresistance observed across commensal Lactobacillus species.
abstract: Lactobacilli are prevalent members of the microbiota in the intestinal and reproductive tracts of humans and other species. They are commonly used in probiotics due to their beneficial effects on human health, including their association with protection from numerous chronic diseases. In addition, these microbes are often prescribed to maintain their presence in the host during antibiotic therapy, as well as to treat diarrhea caused by antibiotics. title: Early-Life Overfeeding Drives Lasting Species-Level Shifts of the Gut Microbiome and Exacerbates Allergic Asthma in Mice.
abstract: Early-life overweight is associated with increased asthma risk in children, but the mechanisms linking metabolic status, the gut microbiome and airway disease remain poorly explored. To address this, we used a litter-size reduction model in mice to examine how early-life overfeeding and overweight shape gut microbial development and later allergic asthma severity. title: Population-scale identification of gut commensals that antagonize antibiotic-resistant pathogens.
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance poses a global threat, yet microbiome-encoded defenses against antibiotic resistance gene (ARG)-associated pathogens remain poorly defined. Here, we analyze 12,238 human gut metagenomes and prioritize 159 commensal species ("coexcluders") that show inverse associations with ARG-associated pathogenic taxa. title: A putative model of the gut-muscle axis in aged livestock
abstract: The gut-muscle axis has been proposed to link gut microbiota with skeletal muscle physiology, yet its universality across livestock species remains unclear. Using aged laying hens, a livestock model with a relatively short digestive tract, we examined the gut microbiota, faecal metabolome, and breast-muscle metabolome by integrative multi-omics analyses in hens fed a Caldifermentibacillus hisashii-containing fermented feed or a control diet. title: The Gut Microbiota-Bile Acid Axis as a Candidate Mechanism for Acupuncture-Related Metabolic Responses in Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: Disease Evidence, Mechanistic Clues, and Causal Gaps.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction in polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is heterogeneous and cannot be explained by obesity alone. The gut microbiota-bile acid axis offers a potential link between intestinal microbial metabolism, enterohepatic feedback, and host metabolic regulation. This mechanism-oriented narrative review integrates human PCOS studies, PCOS-specific experimental models, acupuncture studies, and mechanistic evidence from other metabolic settings. title: The gut microbiome–bile acid-FXR interplay: a pivotal axis in metabolic and gastrointestinal diseases
abstract: ABSTRACT The gut microbiota is increasingly recognized as an essential metabolic “organ”, involved not only in nutrient extraction and energy metabolism but also in generating diverse bioactive metabolites. Among these metabolites, bile acids (BAs) - initially synthesized in the liver - are substantially modified by bacterial enzymes in the gut, enabling them to engage various host signaling pathways. title: Bile acid sequestration reveals microbiome remodeling that dominates FXR signaling to shape host responses to enteric infection
abstract: Approximately 90 million American adults are hypercholesterolemic, with an estimated 43 million individuals either already using or eligible to receive cholesterol-lowering medications, such as bile acid sequestrants. Although bile acid sequestrants have demonstrated therapeutic efficacy in lowering cholesterol levels in individuals with hypercholesterolemia, their impact on intestinal homeostasis in healthy individuals and those with enteric microbial infections remains unclear. title: The interplay between bile acid metabolism and gut microbiome in biliary tract cancers
abstract: The gut microbiota and bile acids (BAs) exist in a tightly regulated, bidirectional relationship that influences host metabolism, immune function, and disease. Primary BAs synthesized in the liver are chemically transformed by intestinal microbes into a diverse pool of secondary BAs, which exert antimicrobial effects and activate host signaling pathways including Farnesoid X Receptor (FXR), Takeda G protein–coupled receptor 5 (TGR5), and sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 2 (S1PR2). title: Pharmacomicrobiomics of GLP-1 receptor agonist gastrointestinal tolerability: integrating host genetics and the gut microbiome
abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) adverse events, such as nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and constipation, remain a dominant barrier to the sustained use of GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), driving discontinuation independently of the drug’s metabolic benefits. title: The sex hormone-gut microbiome axis: mechanistic drivers of sex-disparate bacterial infection outcomes and precision clinical interventions
abstract: SUMMARY Sex disparities in bacterial infections pose significant challenges in clinical microbiology, influencing diagnostic approaches, antimicrobial stewardship, and patient outcomes. abstract: This integrated review synthesizes current evidence on the molecular interplay between the gut microbiome and circadian rhythms, emphasizing a sophisticated bidirectional communication system crucial for maintaining metabolic, immune, and neurological homeostasis. title: Bile Acid Signaling in Metabolic and Inflammatory Diseases and Drug Development
abstract: Bile acids are the end products of cholesterol catabolism. Hepatic bile acid synthesis accounts for a major fraction of daily cholesterol turnover in humans. abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic, disabling and incurable autoimmune disease. It has been widely recognized that gut microbial dysbiosis is an important contributor to the pathogenesis of RA, although distinct alterations in microbiota have been associated with this disease. abstract: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) is a female pregnancy-specific disorder that is characterized by increased serum bile acid and adverse fetal outcomes. The aetiology and mechanism of ICP are poorly understood; thus, existing therapies have been largely empiric. abstract: Adherent-invasive Escherichia coli (AIEC) is a subtype of pathogenic E. coli associated with Crohn's disease. abstract: Caloric restriction diets are a common diet strategy to reduce excess weight and obesity.
